was: Camping at the state-operated South Dakota State Fairgrounds in Huron; 1,200+ electric/water sites plus 50 full-hookup, restrooms/showers - the state's largest campground, open year-round (nightly self-contained FCFS at the gate; fair-week package reservations via the admin office). --Claude

was: City of Mitchell campground on the shore of Lake Mitchell ~5 mi N of downtown. 48 full-hookup RV sites (30/50-amp W/E/S) + 9 tent sites; online reservations plus some first-come, first-served sites daily. Open year-round (water off mid-Oct to late Apr). --Claude

was: Municipal park campground off US-212 on the south side of town by the ballfield and pool; 3 grassy RV sites (RV only, no tents) each with 30-amp electric, plus water pump, dump station, restroom/shower; first-come, first-served (iron-ranger donations, 3-day limit). --Claude

was: City of Faith municipal park (Meade County); ~12 back-in RV sites off a paved loop with 20/30-amp electric and shared water spigots, dump station; sites accommodate ~40 ft. First-come, first-served, self-pay iron ranger, ~$10/night. --Claude

was: City of Aberdeen park campground; 15 RV sites with electric (recently upgraded to 50-amp), modern showers/restrooms, dump station. First-come, first-served (no reservations), open Apr 1-Oct 31. Set in a 25-acre city park with tennis/basketball courts and playground. --Claude

was: Campbell County campground on the shore of Lake Pocasse near Pollock. About 13 RV-capable sites (plus tent/no-hookup sites), primitive: pit toilets, fire rings, grills, tables, playground and a boat ramp; max RV length ~32 ft. Open May-Sep, roughly $5/day; drive-in, reservations by phone with FCFS otherwise. --Claude

was: City of Clear Lake (Deuel County) lakeside park on the east shore of Clear Lake. 24 sites: 10 with water & 30-amp electric and 14 full-hookup (50/30/20-amp) sites, each with table and fire pit; restrooms/showers, boat and fishing docks, disc golf, playground, nature trail; accommodates rigs to ~40 ft. First-come, first-served (city office 605-874-2121). --Claude

About 10 primitive campsites, 5 with electric, on the reservoir's peninsula; one water spigot, one vault toilet, boat ramp and two fishing piers. First-come, first-served (donations encouraged); 5-day stay limit. Open May-Oct. --Claude

was: Rustic drive-in campground on Strawberry Lake in Turtle Mountain State Forest, NE of Bottineau; run by the ND Forest Service. Self-registration; two drinking-water wells, vault toilets, boat ramp, fishing pier, picnic and group areas; no hookups. $15/night cash, first-come, first-served. 'Park next to your site' drive-in loops; most sites are small but reviews note a few fit larger tents/campers (verify length for big rigs). Trout lake, gas motors prohibited. --Claude

Odd-numbered sites reservable May-Sep on recreation.gov, remainder first-come; all FCFS off-season. Pull-through sites 32/42/43/49 take bigger rigs, but trees and tight turns make it challenging over ~35 ft. --Claude

was: USFS Little Missouri National Grassland (Dakota Prairie Grasslands), Medora RD. 10 FCFS single sites for tents/trailers/RVs with picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilet, seasonal hand-pump water. Reached by ~16 mi of gravel/dirt roads off I-94 Exit 10 (grassland roads can be impassable when wet). Near the Maah Daah Hey/Buffalo Gap trails; Camels Hump Lake along the exit road. Hitching rails for horses but general drive-in sites too (not equestrian-only). --Claude

was: Lisbon Park District park on the Sheyenne River, open April 1 to November 14: a West Campground of full-hookup sites and a North Campground behind the FEMA dike with electric and water, every site wired for 20, 30 and 50 amps, plus primitive camping on the grass.  The campground is self-service: hookup sites must be reserved and paid ahead, while primitive sites are first come, first served.  There are showerhouses and a dump station, and the park has an outdoor pool, mini golf, a skate park, ball fields and courts. --Claude
